Series::tril_¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::tril_() const -> Series&
Series::tril_(std::int64_t diagonal) const -> Series&

What It Does¶

tril_() is the in-place sibling of tril().

It applies the same lower-triangular masking rule, but instead of returning a fresh value it mutates the receiver and returns the same handle by reference.

That difference matters in three places:

  • later reads from the same object see the zeroed result

  • aliasing handles to the same storage see the same mutation

  • mutation-sensitive state such as storage_version() changes

Overload Map¶

tril_()

Equivalent to tril_(0).

tril_(std::int64_t diagonal)

Mutating lower-triangular masking with an explicit keep boundary.

Parameters¶

diagonal (std::int64_t)

The highest diagonal that remains non-zero after the mutation.

Returns¶

Series& The same Series, after in-place mutation.

Examples¶

Example 1. tril_() mutates the receiver and bumps its storage version.

auto square = pluss::make_series({
    {1, 2, 3},
    {4, 5, 6},
    {7, 8, 9},
}, pluss::ScalarType::Int64);

std::cout << "before=" << square.storage_version() << "\n";
square.tril_(1);
std::cout << "after=" << square.storage_version() << "\n";
std::cout << square;

Output¶

before=0
after=1
pluss::Series(shape=[3,3], strides=[3,1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=9, contiguous=true)
data=[[1, 2, 0],
  [4, 5, 6],
  [7, 8, 9]]

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • tril_() mutates. Use tril() if you need value semantics.

  • The zero-argument form is just the main-diagonal case.

  • Storage-version-sensitive code can use storage_version() to detect the mutation.

Summary¶

Use tril_() when the lower-triangular mask should become the new state of the current Series, not just a derived copy.
